investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-24T12:46–12:54Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported it as Insufficient, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node in the 6-node cluster can accept a new peer-pod VM at this time. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already at capacity even if the cluster has other nodes.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM quota or limit set too low for the current workload volume: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource may have a hard cap per node that has been reached, possibly due to leaked or long-running agent VMs from prior eval runs not being cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883).
Lower confidence — transient spike in concurrent remote agent demand at the time of the eval run (12:46–12:54Z) temporarily exhausted capacity that would otherwise be available.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 12:49 and 12:54 UTC on 2026-07-24 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents swarm backend has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is consistent across all three sibling checks, indicating the eval pod could not be placed on any node. The runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which requires a kata peer-pod VM slot; with no slot available the pod remained Unschedulable for ~145 s before the check timed out. This is an eval-infrastructure failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, so even if other nodes had capacity they cannot be used. The '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' message confirms this constraint is in effect and limits the blast radius of any VM slot shortage.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent eval load: with only 2 kata-capable nodes, any overlap between scheduled eval runs or production remote-agent workloads can saturate capacity. No preemption victims were found, suggesting no lower-priority pods were available to evict.

investigation.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 711 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigation.summary: The eval fetched the published snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json and measured snapshotAgeMinutes=711, which is 2.37× the contract maximum of 300 minutes (5 hours). This is a localized eval failure against the published-observability-snapshot check; all three sibling public-website checks passed, confirming the public web surface itself is reachable and this failure is isolated to snapshot freshness.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json to https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 711 minutes (~11.85 hours) as of the eval run at 2026-07-24T12:54:12Z. The snapshot file is structurally valid and was previously produced by a real workflow run (source=github-actions, hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true), but it has not been refreshed within the 300-minute window required by the expected-output contract. The root cause is a missed or failed scheduled workflow execution, not a problem with the snapshot schema, the eval runner logic, or the public website serving infrastructure.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed with HTTP 200 responses — the public website and /observability route are reachable; the failure is isolated to snapshot content freshness.

possibleCauses: Most likely — The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that publishes status.json was skipped, cancelled, or failed silently approximately 711+ minutes before the eval ran, leaving the previously published file in place without a refresh.

Second — The workflow ran but the GitHub Pages publish step failed (e.g., a Pages deployment error, branch push conflict, or permissions issue), so the old file remained at the CDN URL despite a workflow execution.
Third — The workflow schedule was inadvertently disabled, removed, or its cron trigger was not met (e.g., a repository setting change or Actions billing/quota limit paused scheduled runs).
Fourth — A transient GitHub Actions runner availability issue caused the scheduled job to be queued but never executed during the affected window.

Lower likelihood — The snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the runner (statusSnapshotEvidence) has a bug that overstates age; however, the 711-minute value is far outside the 300-minute threshold and the snapshot's own generatedAtPresent=true field is consistent with a genuinely old file.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-24T12:46–12:54Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported it as Insufficient, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node in the 6-node cluster can accept a new peer-pod VM at this time. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 12:49 and 12:54 UTC on 2026-07-24 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents swarm backend has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is consistent across all three sibling checks, indicating the eval pod could not be placed on any node. The runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which requires a kata peer-pod VM slot; with no slot available the pod remained Unschedulable for ~145 s before the check timed out. This is an eval-infrastructure failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval pod. Supported by the identical scheduler message across all three sibling checks spanning ~5 minutes.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, so even if other nodes had capacity they cannot be used. The '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' message confirms this constraint is in effect and limits the blast radius of any VM slot shortage.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent eval load: with only 2 kata-capable nodes, any overlap between scheduled eval runs or production remote-agent workloads can saturate capacity. No preemption victims were found, suggesting no lower-priority pods were available to evict.

Lower confidence — transient spike in production remote-agent usage consuming VM slots at the time of the eval run: no user-traffic signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this cannot be confirmed or ruled out from the packet alone.

investigations.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 711 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigations.summary: The eval fetched the published snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json and measured snapshotAgeMinutes=711, which is 2.37× the contract maximum of 300 minutes (5 hours). This is a localized eval failure against the published-observability-snapshot check; all three sibling public-website checks passed, confirming the public web surface itself is reachable and this failure is isolated to snapshot freshness.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json to https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 711 minutes (~11.85 hours) as of the eval run at 2026-07-24T12:54:12Z. The snapshot file is structurally valid and was previously produced by a real workflow run (source=github-actions, hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true), but it has not been refreshed within the 300-minute window required by the expected-output contract. The root cause is a missed or failed scheduled workflow execution, not a problem with the snapshot schema, the eval runner logic, or the public website serving infrastructure.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=711, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true, generatedAtPresent=true — all other assertions pass; only the age assertion fails.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check config shows statusImpact='informational' and required=false — this failure does not constitute a required check outage.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed with HTTP 200 responses — the public website and /observability route are reachable; the failure is isolated to snapshot content freshness.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2164-2172: runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives evidence via statusSnapshotEvidence(payload) — the runner correctly read the live remote file; the staleness is in the file itself, not the eval runner.
possibleCauses: Most likely — The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that publishes status.json was skipped, cancelled, or failed silently approximately 711+ minutes before the eval ran, leaving the previously published file in place without a refresh.

Second — The workflow ran but the GitHub Pages publish step failed (e.g., a Pages deployment error, branch push conflict, or permissions issue), so the old file remained at the CDN URL despite a workflow execution.
Third — The workflow schedule was inadvertently disabled, removed, or its cron trigger was not met (e.g., a repository setting change or Actions billing/quota limit paused scheduled runs).
Fourth — A transient GitHub Actions runner availability issue caused the scheduled job to be queued but never executed during the affected window.

Lower likelihood — The snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the runner (statusSnapshotEvidence) has a bug that overstates age; however, the 711-minute value is far outside the 300-minute threshold and the snapshot's own generatedAtPresent=true field is consistent with a genuinely old file.
